sources.entry: ShazamScrobbler - Scrobble vinyl, radios, movies to Last.fm.

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu-bar style helper that takes songs Shazam has identified and scrobbles them to Last.fm, keeping a playback history.
summary.what_it_does: The app works alongside the Shazam Mac app. When Shazam tags a song playing around the user, ShazamScrobbler submits that track to Last.fm as a scrobble, so the listening history stays up to date. The README says it requires Shazam to have tagged at least one song before the first launch. Release builds are universal (Apple silicon and Intel) and need macOS 11 or later. Published builds are code signed and notarized by a maintainer before being attached to GitHub releases. The README describes an uninstall process that deletes its defaults entry and the app bundle. Dependencies named in the README include the Last.fm SDK by gangverk, FMDB, and LaunchAtLoginController by Ben Clark-Robinson.
use_cases: keep a Last.fm history of music played around me
log songs from vinyl or radio that Shazam recognizes
automatically record Shazam tags on a Mac
install a Shazam-to-Last.fm bridge on Apple silicon
remove the app and its preferences cleanly
how_to_run: Install the Shazam Mac app and let it tag at least one song.
Download ShazamScrobbler.dmg from the GitHub releases (about 1 MB).
Open the DMG and drag ShazamScrobbler into Applications.
Launch ShazamScrobbler and connect it to your Last.fm account.
notable: Works from Shazam's tags rather than audio capture, so it needs no separate listening step
Universal release builds run natively on M-series Macs without Rosetta
Release builds are code signed and notarized by a maintainer
Simple uninstall path documented in the README
caveats: Requires the Shazam Mac app to be installed and to have tagged at least one song before first launch
Only scrobbles to Last.fm; no other services are named in the README
